decisions.note: The members are intentionally retained version-specific Zstandard sources; sharing code across the historical copies would defeat their independent compatibility boundaries.
Both spell-tree walks duplicate the same byte-array binary search and child transition; a helper can own that coherent operation while callers keep their distinct whitespace behavior.
Connection, read, and write paths repeat the same OpenSSL error classification and reporting sequence, which has a natural shared diagnostic-helper boundary.
The adjacent parser setup blocks perform the same node construction and attachment flow while varying the markdown/item inputs, making the variation explicit as parameters.
Three maintained network tests copy the complete slab allocation callback; one test-support callback can serve all three without hiding scenario behavior.
The command lifecycle cases exercise different Before, After, and shell-completion semantics; their common command construction is boilerplate around independently meaningful scenarios.
Two integration tests duplicate the embedded server, client, snapshot, and cleanup sequence, which can be returned by one scoped test harness.
The large color-theme literals repeat a stable default field set and vary a bounded palette; a base table plus explicit overrides would remove substantial duplication.
The event and logger packages carry the same Kafka SCRAM client implementation; an internal shared package can own the mechanism without changing either caller.
Adjacent cookie tests repeat construction and assertions while varying cookie attributes, a direct table-driven test case.
The overlap is a Java import list; each compilation unit must declare the names it uses and there is no behavioral abstraction to extract.
The single- and double-quoted tokenizer states duplicate the same scan/escape/termination logic and differ primarily in the terminating quote character.
The hundreds of members are SWIG-generated Java wrappers, so the repeated binding scaffolding is not maintained as hand-refactorable application code.
The detected family consists of repeated imports in independent test compilation units and exposes no reusable behavior.
The match is a four-line accessor required on distinct parser subclasses; an extra indirection would not remove the per-class method contract.
The two TimeDelta microsecond cases repeat setup and assertions and vary only the input/expected boundary values, fitting one parameterized test.
Each member is a two-line teardown in a separate test class; a shared base or helper would add coupling for negligible code removal.
Distribution tests repeat the same seeded sample-consistency loop; a shared assertion helper can accept the distribution and expected samples.
urlutils explicitly embeds a dated OrderedMultiDict snapshot from dictutils to remain self-contained; sharing its prelude would undo that deliberate frozen-copy boundary.
The application and sans-I/O application modules duplicate the same type variables and timedelta conversion helper, which belong in their shared internal support layer.
Adjacent cdpath examples repeat the same stub, chdir expectation, and Pry command while varying only the selected path case.
Six UI-macro conversion tests duplicate header construction, conversion, and suffix assertion while varying only macro input and expected rendering.
The duplicated HTML fragments are independent expected-output cases in a parser fixture; consolidating them would erase the literal expectations being specified.
Two related release tests contain the exact same nontrivial teardown lifecycle, which can live in their common test base.
ForloopDrop and TableRowLoopDrop duplicate the same index, reverse-index, first, and last behavior over identical state, a clear shared loop-drop abstraction.
The overlap is a small Rust use list shared by exporter modules; each module still needs its own imports and no computation is duplicated.
The memchr implementation is duplicated across tokio and tokio-util crate boundaries so each crate can use it without introducing a reverse or cyclic dependency.
Both members are two-line lines-count getters on different domain types; extracting the arithmetic would cost more than it removes.
Heap and metadata recovery copy the same external sync invocation and failure logging, a coherent recovery helper with one outcome.
The family is a two-line milliseconds convenience function spread across independent test targets and one internal module; centralizing it would add more dependency surface than code.
The visual scenes independently specify bitmap, tagged, split, and ordinary text rendering; their shared style is setup around intentionally separate renderer fixtures.
The repeated table markup is literal expected output for two parser cases in one golden fixture, not maintained behavior that can be shared.
Four retry tests repeat server setup, failing response, request options, rejection, and count assertions while varying status/method inputs.
The locale objects are declarative per-language definitions whose shared fields are the required schema and whose options are the variant payload, not duplicated behavior.
Each marble test specifies a different operator's never-emitting behavior; a cross-operator helper would obscure the independent public contracts for little setup reduction.
The similar bodies are required public overloads on distinct constrained UI extensions, with different placeholder and image-access semantics delegated into their specialized parsed-options paths.
These Resource overloads are thin public API delegations that convert to Source; the per-type signatures must remain and extracting the few statements would not remove them.
The files are successive authored documentation tutorial stages whose shared viewDidLoad prefix intentionally preserves each independently compilable step.
The require family exposes distinct sync/async and closure/autoclosure public overloads with different generic return contracts; their construction is intentional API symmetry.
The package manifests intentionally target different Swift tools versions and must remain standalone inputs to SwiftPM even while their current contents overlap.
Three polling requirement paths copy the full execute/poll/verify orchestration; a shared internal operation can accept the matcher and final verification behavior.
The repeated parameter tables are generated Jazzy HTML and duplicated docset output, not source maintained for manual refactoring.
The breadcrumbs and navigation wrappers are generated Jazzy pages, including mirrored docset copies.
The common headers are generated documentation chrome repeated across HTML and docset pages.
The members are generated documentation page headers rather than Swift product source.
The large repeated navigation lists are generated documentation output shared across hundreds of pages.
The repeated RxSwift navigation blocks are generated HTML, not an authored abstraction opportunity.
Core and global counter tests repeat the same concurrent stress sequence and differ only in how the Counter obtains its factory.
Recorder concurrency tests duplicate setup, dispatch-group recording, and count assertions with only factory construction varying.
Timer concurrency tests copy the complete stress harness across core and global systems and can share a parameterized constructor.
Six test targets duplicate the same timed polling assertion implementation; NIO test support can own one shared assertion helper.
Each standalone example handler must implement errorCaught, and the shared body is only a print plus close operation whose extraction would leave every required method in place.
NIOFS and _NIOFileSystem expose the same FileType across separate module/API boundaries during migration; sharing the public definition would collapse the compatibility boundary.
Seven lifecycle tests repeat a long run, iterator, signal, ping, and staged-shutdown scenario while varying service configuration and terminal ordering.
Two related test classes copy the full configurable ServiceGroup factory; one test-support constructor can serve both.
Three tests repeat the same staged service-exit and liveness assertion sequence; a helper can drive the iterators and services while preserving each test's final outcome.
